note: Workflow eval tasks: whole requests run through the full harness (every agent.tool and tool family), starting from the entry point named in `surface` (an agent.entry). Cursor tasks carry every display's screenshot from the start, as the cursor captures on every request; `start.screen` names the cursor display's fixture. Fixture tasks use the pages in ../browser/sites and the fixture search index; live tasks use real engines, sites and the accounts in `requires`. `expect` strings must all appear in the final answer; a rubric is graded by the judge. `tools.required` must each be called at least once and `tools.forbidden` never (a trailing * matches a family). `maxCalls` counts tool calls, `maxRuns` counts runs started for the request (screen hand-offs start new runs today). Tool names are the singular agent names from docs/plans/agent-harness.md as the model sees them (`agent_tool_use`, `memory_pref_*`, `memory_history_*`, `integration_*`); until phase 2 renames the tools, the runner translates them to today's names in its own table, since the plan keeps no aliases. Prompts keep the person's own words ("my Space", "my note"), which the agent must resolve through the glossary. `web_fetch` does not exist yet (docs/plans/agent-harness.md, phase 1); until it does, tasks that require it score as failures, which is the baseline. `state` lists what the runner reads back after an account task (a Composio tool or a Misty API path, with {{placeholders}}); the judge grades against that end state. `approve` lists app actions the task explicitly asks for; the runner approves their cards like the person would, and any other card still ends the run. `truth` is the answer key the judge gets: facts about the seeded data that the rubric is checked against. A check with `since` shows only items created or changed during the run, and `undo` removes what the run created once it is graded, so every run starts from the seeded state.
